newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan vegoil rates seen lower on good crop.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan vegoil rates seen lower on good crop.

text.p: Pakistani vegetable oil rates are expected to slip in next trading week as international prices tumbled on reports of good vegoil crops and a depressed Asian demand, dealers said on Saturday.

"Vegoil prices fell abroad as there has been a good soybean crop in the United States, while in Malaysia people also expect an increased production," dealer Kamran Ahmed said. "There were no tenders from China, India and Pakistan for the last two weeks, which also depressed the prices abroad."
Ahmed said Pakistan's production of cottonseed, a major local source of edible oil, had been good this year.

Dealers said Pakistan's vegoil stocks slipped to 111,000 tonnes last week from 122,000 a week earlier. RBD palm oil and palm olein stocks fell to 90,000 tonnes from 98,000 tonnes last week and soyabean and sunflower oil to 17,000 from 19,000 tonnes.

The Ghee Corp of Pakistan has a stock of 4,000 tonnes of palm oil and palm olien compared to 5,000 last week. It booked orders by October 10 for the import of 9,000 tonnes of RBD palm oil and palm olein.
One ship is now unloading 14,120 tonnes of palm oil at Port Qasim, near Karachi, while another carrying about 20,000 tonnes of Palm oil is expected to arrive by October 18.

One ship carrying 10,100 tonnes of soybean oil will arrive by October 20 and another, with a similar load by October 28. One ship was is loading 25,000 tonnes of palm oil at a Malaysian port while another was is loading around 10,000 tonnes of soybean oil at a South American port, a dealer said.
